content:
The late Princess Diana's brother, Charles Spencer, has recently spoken publicly about the ongoing rift between Princes William and Harry.

Speaking in an interview with the BBC, Spencer said: "From what the media has reported, people might think I lean towards Harry's side, but actually I stand on the side of my late sister's two sons — I support them both." The interview aired on Sunday, coinciding with the publication of his new book about Diana, "The Swan Song: Diana, My Sister."

The historian added: "Whatever either of them needs, I will offer the same support. I never intervene on either side — I just want to be a positive presence."

Speaking about the broken relationship between Harry and William, Spencer said the situation had "reached this point" and that "both sides have many reasons."

He shared: "I hope that one day they can reconcile, but I don't know the full picture. I'm certainly not aware of the more detailed parts, so if I intervene too much, I would feel I am overstepping. All I want to say is that, as a mother, of course one would hope the two sons can get along happily and love each other."

Spencer was recently interviewed by People magazine, where he also addressed another topic of great interest to royal watchers: when he informed the two princes about the book.

Spencer said: "I told them at the same time — that's all I can say. The four people — William, Harry, and my two sisters Sarah and Jane — I told them all at the same time. What I can say is that Harry had absolutely no problem with it."

The historian shared: "He [Harry] said he hoped there wouldn't be anything in the book that would embarrass him. I replied and said 'no.' I think they had actually been worried about my intentions in writing this book all along." He added that the book "essentially ends with Diana's death in 1997."

He added: "I can assure them both that they will of course appear in the book, but mainly as examples of two little boys who had the most wonderful mother. I have not invaded their privacy in any way at all."

Spencer's book was published on Tuesday, just ahead of the 30th anniversary of Diana's death on 31 August 1997.
